extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders searching Federal Register documents about the CHIPS Act (industry applicants, grant recipients, state/local governments, legal counsel, notice-and-comment participants)
extracted.subtask_description: A search-results/index page listing Federal Register documents that reference the CHIPS Act; includes titles, abstracts, and excerpts of notices, rules, information-collection requests, and other CHIPS-related Federal actions useful to commenters and applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act public comment period for information collections
rubrics_metrics.description: For information collection notices submitted under the PRA, the Department invites the general public and other Federal agencies to comment for 60 days preceding submission of the collection to OMB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears across multiple entries (e.g., "invites the general public and other Federal agencies to comment on proposed and continuing information collections...allow for 60 days of public comment preceding submission to OMB"). Use this period to submit burdens, needs/uses, and burden-estimate comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Advisory Committee Act meeting openness and notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory committee meetings (e.g., Industrial Advisory Committee) are governed by the Federal Advisory Committee Act and must provide public notice, be open to the public, and post final agendas on agency websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excerpt: "Pursuant to the Federal Advisory Committee Act...notice is hereby given that the Industrial Advisory Committee will have a meeting...and will be open to the public." Agencies post background information and final agendas (e.g., NIST chips industrial-advisory-committee page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Manufacturing Investment Credit eligibility and rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations implementing the advanced manufacturing investment credit (sections 48D and 50) set the eligibility requirements taxpayers must meet to claim the credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations adopt with modifications proposed rules and state applicability dates; reviewers/applicants should consult the full TD for specific eligibility criteria and applicability (§ references provided in notices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special 10-year credit recapture rule for material expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: A special 10-year credit recapture rule applies if there is a significant transaction involving the material expansion of semiconductor manufacturing capacity in a foreign country of concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As described in the Advanced Manufacturing Investment Credit final rule excerpts: the recapture rule is triggered by defined transactions involving material expansion in a foreign country of concern—details and triggers are in the final regs (TD references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'material expansion' includes construction of new facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department revised the definition of 'material expansion' to clarify that construction of new semiconductor manufacturing facilities falls within the scope of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excerpt: "amending the definition of 'material expansion'...to clarify that the construction of new semiconductor manufacturing facilities falls within the scope of the rule." This affects when prohibitions/recapture rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing improper use of CHIPS Act funding — prohibitions, definitions, notification, enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule implements Act conditions to prevent CHIPS funding from directly or indirectly benefiting foreign countries of concern by defining relevant terms, describing prohibited activities, and setting procedures for notifying the Secretary of non-compliance and enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excerpt: "defines terms related to these conditions, describes the types of activities that are prohibited by those conditions, and sets forth procedures for notifying the Secretary of Commerce of non-compliance and the process by which the Secretary will enforce these provisions." For applicants and recipients, compliance obligations are defined in the rule text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient reporting obligations for CHIPS awards (mandatory, recurring quarterly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient reporting is mandatory to receive and maintain CHIPS Act funding and is required on a recurring quarterly submission schedule during the lifespan of an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excerpt: "Frequency: Recurring during lifespan of an award on quarterly submission schedule." "Respondent's Obligation: Mandatory to receive and maintain CHIPS Act funding." Reports are part of the Recipient Reporting ICR and specify data and cadence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Davis-Bacon and Related Acts compliance for CHIPS-funded construction
rubrics_metrics.description: CHIPS-related funding that involves construction is subject to Davis-Bacon and Related Acts compliance requirements; agencies issue ICRs to collect compliance-related information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excerpt from a Davis-Bacon ICR: the Department invites PRA comments and identifies the Operations Specialist contact; applicants/recipients should be prepared to meet wage-determination and certified payroll obligations where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental review requirements: Programmatic Environmental Assessment and FONSI for modernization/internal expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: NIST issued a Programmatic Environmental Assessment (PEA) and a Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI) for the modernization and expansion (or internal expansion within existing footprints) of semiconductor fabrication facilities under the CHIPS Incentives Program; draft PEAs are posted for public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excerpts: Final and Draft PEA notices explain scope (modernization/internal expansion within existing footprints), provide opportunity for public comment (for drafts), and describe that a FONSI has been issued for covered activities. Commenters should address environmental impacts within the PEA scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation of outside advisors for technical, legal, market, and real-estate issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The CHIPS Incentives Program may solicit outside advisors to provide expertise on audits, insurance, market reviews, legal matters, real estate, and other technical issues via a formal information-collection request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excerpt: "The requests will be used by the CHIPS Incentives Program...audits, insurance, market reviews, legal, real estate, and other technical issues." Firms responding to such solicitations should expect to supply credentials and scope-of-work information as specified in the ICR/solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Intent/Notice of Funding Opportunity procedures for CHIPS R&D competitions
rubrics_metrics.description: CHIPS R&D posts Notices of Intent (NOIs) and NOFOs to announce upcoming competitions, provide contact points, and allow applicants time to form collaborations; questions/responses may be posted on the CHIPS R&D website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excerpt: "This NOI is provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations...Responses to questions received...will be posted on the CHIPS R&D website." Applicants should monitor the stated contact points and the CHIPS funding-opportunities page for updates and Q&As.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative metadata included in ICR notices (burden estimates, affected public, legal authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information-collection notices include administrative rubric items such as number of respondents, average hours per response, total burden hours, affected public, respondent obligation, frequency, and the legal authority (e.g., CHIPS Act citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in excerpts: "Number of Respondents: 56. Average Hours per Response: 10 hours. Burden Hours: 560 hours. Affected Public: Business or other for-profit organizations. Respondent's Obligation: Mandatory to receive and maintain CHIPS Act funding. Legal Authority: CHIPS Act of 2022." These metrics set expectations for response burden and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of authority for CHIPS Act functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may publish delegation of authorities conferred by the CHIPS Act (e.g., delegation to State Department officers to approve transfers for CHIPS international technology security programs), specifying scope and statutory basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excerpt: delegation pursuant to section 1 of the State Department Basic Authorities Act and section 102(c) of the CHIPS Act; practitioners should consult delegation notices to identify who may exercise statutory functions and approvals.
